oewn-02629987-v.learner: to develop into something clear and separate of its own.
examples: Over the years the scattered farms formed into a small town.

oewn-01663142-v.learner: to make something, usually so that it can do a particular job.
examples: He formed a hook out of a piece of wire to pull the key from the drain.

oewn-00144670-v.learner: to take on a form or shape.
examples: As you knead it, the dough slowly forms into a smooth ball.

oewn-02435769-v.learner: to fix something firmly in someone's mind.
examples: What he saw that night was formed so deeply in his mind that he never forgot it.

oewn-01085437-v.learner: to give up because you are beaten or have no hope left; to admit that you have lost.
examples: They were losing by ten points, but the team never quit.

oewn-02232269-v.learner: to turn away from something and give it up.
examples: He quit his claim to the land and let his brother have it.

oewn-01645979-v.learner: to bring something new into a place or situation.
examples: The new manager introduced a simpler way of keeping the accounts.

oewn-01067137-v.learner: to show a person or thing, such as an actor or a song, to the public for the first time.
examples: The band introduced a new song at the concert.

oewn-00708522-v.learner: to put something before an official group of people.
examples: The senator introduced a bill to lower taxes.

oewn-00903562-v.learner: to give something an opening part that comes before the main part.
examples: He introduced the book with a short note to the reader.

oewn-00187671-v.learner: to put, fit, or push something into something else.
examples: The doctor introduced a thin tube into the vein.

oewn-01424276-v.learner: to put something into something else.
examples: She introduced a few jokes into her speech.

oewn-00350246-v.learner: to come before something and lead the way to it.
examples: The steam engine introduced an age of factories.

oewn-07485811-n.learner: an official contest in which two or more people or teams compete.
examples: We watched the tennis match on Saturday.

oewn-03734302-n.learner: a thing that is exactly the same as another thing.
examples: The copy was a perfect match of the original painting.

oewn-05703985-n.learner: something that looks like another thing, or goes well with it.
examples: Those blue shoes are a good match for your dress.

oewn-09649426-n.learner: a person who has the same standing as another person in a group.
examples: In the whole school, she had no match at chess.

oewn-03734473-n.learner: a piece of wood or cardboard that is on fire.
examples: He dropped the lit match into the dry leaves.

oewn-13617916-n.learner: the score you need to win a match.
examples: One more point and it would be game, set and match.
Thin smoke arose from the chimney.

oewn-01987278-v.learner: to get up onto your feet.
examples: Everyone in the room arose when the judge came in.

oewn-00018151-v.learner: to get up and out of bed.
examples: She arose at six and dressed quickly.

oewn-02589224-v.learner: to take part in a rebellion, or to turn against those you were loyal to before.
examples: The people arose against the cruel king.

oewn-00745330-v.learner: to be in touch with someone, or to get in touch with them.
examples: I tried to reach her by phone all day.

oewn-02691488-v.learner: to stretch as far as a certain point.
examples: The garden reaches all the way down to the river.

oewn-02531751-v.learner: to get something by working hard for it.
examples: After long talks, the two sides finally reached an agreement.

oewn-02235554-v.learner: to put something into someone's hands or care.
examples: Could you reach me that book from the top shelf?

oewn-01148517-v.learner: to try very hard, using a lot of effort or energy.
examples: He reached and strained with all his strength to finish the climb.

oewn-15251247-n.learner: the end of a pregnancy, when a baby is about to be born.
examples: The baby was born at term and was perfectly healthy.

oewn-05864488-n.learner: any one of the separate amounts that make up a polynomial in mathematics.
examples: The expression 3x + 2 has two terms.

oewn-06764688-n.learner: one of the main naming phrases that a statement in logic is built from.
examples: In "all men are mortal", "men" is the subject term.

oewn-04420858-n.learner: in architecture, a statue, a human head and shoulders, or an animal carved out of the top of a square pillar, first used in ancient Rome to mark a boundary.
examples: A stone term stood at each corner of the old garden.

oewn-06800007-n.learner: the written details that show where a place is, put on letters or parcels that are to be delivered there.
examples: She wrote the address clearly on the envelope.

oewn-06807073-n.learner: a sign in front of a house or business that shows the usual way of describing where it is.
examples: The address above the shop door was painted in gold.

oewn-06367922-n.learner: in computing, the code that shows where a piece of information is stored.
examples: The program reads the data stored at that memory address.

oewn-04849463-n.learner: the skill of doing or saying what is right for the occasion.
examples: She handled the awkward guests with great address.

oewn-05089855-n.learner: in golf, the way a player stands when getting ready to hit the ball.
examples: He settled into his address and swung smoothly.

oewn-09907302-n.learner: a person who visits you, for social or business reasons.
examples: Tidy your room, because we are having company tonight.

oewn-08281818-n.learner: a group of people who are together for a time to do something.
examples: A small company of travellers set out at dawn.

oewn-08203951-n.learner: a group of performers and the people who work with them, especially in the theatre.
examples: The theatre company toured the country last year.

oewn-08231193-n.learner: a small army unit, usually made up of two or three platoons.
examples: He was given command of a company of soldiers.

oewn-08235980-n.learner: all the people who work on a ship, including the officers.
examples: The captain called the whole ship's company on deck.

oewn-08094547-n.learner: a group of firefighters together with their equipment.

oewn-15325026-n.learner: the period of time that is thought best for starting or finishing something.
examples: We have a short window to plant the seeds before the first frost.

oewn-04596042-n.learner: in computing, a box on the screen that shows something different from the rest of the screen.

oewn-04596289-n.learner: an opening in a wall or screen that lets in light and air and through which customers can be served.
examples: She paid for her ticket at the window.

oewn-09503207-n.learner: an opening that looks like a window or does the job of one.

oewn-04595890-n.learner: a clear panel set into material you cannot otherwise see through, such as on an envelope.
examples: The address shows through the window of the envelope.
